chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The man pays the Zakat of al-Fitra on behalf of his Mukatab (contracted slave), the slave of his wife, his Christian and Magian slave, and whoever he closes his door upon (i.e., dependents under his roof).

key_terms.رَقِيقِ امْرَأَتِهِ: The slave(s) belonging to his wife
key_terms.زَكَاةَ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitra (the obligatory charity paid at the end of Ramadan)
key_terms.مَا أَغْلَقَ عَلَيْهِ بَابَهُ: Whomever he closes his door upon (dependents under his roof)
key_terms.مُكَاتَبِهِ: His contracted slave (a slave who has agreed to pay a sum for his freedom)

ai.seo_question: Who is eligible for Zakat al-Fitra payment on behalf of others according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the extent of the head of household's financial liability for Zakat al-Fitra, extending beyond free dependents to include specific categories of slaves and non-Muslims under his authority. It highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that the obligation rests on the provider who maintains the household, regardless of the dependents' faith or freedom status, provided they are under his roof. This underscores the social welfare dimension of Fitra as a communal responsibility to ensure the sustenance of all dependents during Eid.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, raising it, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The man would pay the Zakat of the Fitra on behalf of his contracted slaves, and a slave of his wife, and his Christian and Magian slave, and whoever he closes his door upon (other members of his family)’.
en.sarwar: 20. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is permissible to pay Zakat al-Fitrah to a slave who has contracted his freedom, slave of one’s wife, his own Christian, Zoroastrian slave and those who have closed the door on themselves.’”
